messages:
samir: hey team, first day! i tried `kubectl get pods -n billing` after importing the provided kubeconfig and got `Forbidden`. not sure who owns billing namespace. any pointers on who to ask for access?
samir: here's the exact error: `Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User \"samir@redwood.com\" cannot list resource \"pods\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"billing\"`
devops: welcome samir :) quick checks: 1) `kubectl config current-context` to confirm the right context, 2) `kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=billing` to see effective perms. can you paste outputs (no kubeconfigs)?
samir: `kubectl config current-context` -> `prod-samir`
samir: `kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=billing` -> `no`
elaine: hey samir, eng-billing owns that namespace. we use SSO group `eng-billing-devs` for dev access. do you have your SSO mapped to any groups yet? if not, i can raise a short-lived RoleBinding for your user.
samir: my SSO id is samir@redwood.com, github: samirr
elaine: i'll add a RoleBinding with `view` role scoped to `billing` for 24h so you can complete setup. if you need write perms we can file a ticket.
elaine: applying:
```
kubectl create rolebinding rb-onboard-samir-billing -n billing --clusterrole=view --user=samir@redwood.com --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```
elaine: done. retry the `kubectl get pods -n billing`
onboard-bot: FYI the onboarding doc lists the group mapping steps: https://internal.redwood/docs/onboard/kube-access (please follow persistent access request flow if you need >1d access)
samir: works now, pod list shows up. thanks! :tada:
samir: quick follow-up: when i have multiple kubeconfigs merged, what's the safe way to avoid running commands against prod accidentally? any aliases or tips?
devops: prefer `kubectl config use-context` before doing anything. i also recommend `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/.kube/staging` and keep prod separate. my shortcut: `kc() { kubectl --context=\"$1\" \"$@\"; }` then `kc prod get pods`. also add a bash prompt segment showing current context.
samir: great, will update my shell. thanks all!
